title: What If You Started Growing and Couldn't Stop?
description:
What if you started growing, and couldn't stop? From your street to the edge of the observable universe, one continuous journey through every scale, with the real heights and distances of everything you pass.

The premise is impossible. The sizes, distances and signal speeds are real.
core_message: Growing from 1.7 m to the size of the observable universe crosses 26 powers of ten.
comment_question: Where would you have asked to stop?

scenes.narration: You can't stop growing.
What if you started growing, and couldn't stop?
It starts on an ordinary street, on an ordinary morning.
One point seven metres. Then one point eight.
Your shoes split first. Then your jacket.
By the time you notice, you're looking into upstairs windows.
Ten metres. People below are pointing up at you.
You are taller than every house on the street.
And every second, you grow a little faster.
Ninety three metres. As tall as the Statue of Liberty, pedestal and all.
A step that crossed the road now crosses a city block.
Your head is up in the morning haze.
Eight hundred and twenty eight metres. You look the world's tallest building in the eye.
And then it's below you.
Here's the strange part. Your nerves carry signals at about a hundred metres a second.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: So a message from your feet now takes twenty five seconds to reach your brain.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: You're walking on feet you can't feel in real time.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Clouds drift around your knees.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Eight thousand eight hundred and forty nine metres. You're as tall as Mount Everest.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Eleven kilometres. Airliners cruise past your face.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: The sky above you is turning dark.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: One hundred kilometres. The edge of space.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Your head has left the atmosphere. Your feet are still in a city.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Four hundred kilometres. The space station passes your ear.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Stub your toe now, and you'll feel it an hour and a half later.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Each of your feet covers a country. You can't tell which ones.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Twelve thousand seven hundred kilometres. You're as tall as the Earth is wide.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Everyone you have ever met is somewhere under your feet.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: The whole planet is a ball you could hold, if you could still bend down.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Three hundred and eighty four thousand kilometres. The Moon drifts past your shoulder.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Apollo astronauts took three days to cross that gap. You grew it in seconds.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: A message from your toe now takes months to arrive.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: One point four million kilometres. The Sun is smaller than you are.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: Three hundred million kilometres. Earth's whole orbit would fit inside you.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: A signal from your feet would take ninety five years. Longer than a human life.
scenes.gauge_label: A signal from your feet

scenes.narration: And here's the problem. Even light takes time to cross you now.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Light leaving your feet reaches your eyes almost an hour later.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Nine billion kilometres. Neptune's orbit, the edge of the planets.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Voyager one, the farthest thing humans ever built, is somewhere near your waist.
scenes.landmark_note: about 25 billion km from the Sun
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: It left Earth in nineteen seventy seven. You passed it in a heartbeat.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: The Sun is now a speck of dust somewhere inside you.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: One light-year. Light takes a whole year to climb you.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Four point two light-years. The nearest star, Proxima Centauri.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Hundreds of stars are inside you now. Then thousands.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: If you stubbed your toe today, you'd feel it in the year three thousand.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Everyone you knew has been gone for centuries.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Below you, a thin bright band appears. It's the disc of our galaxy.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: A hundred thousand light-years. The Milky Way. All of it.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Hundreds of billions of stars. One of them was yours.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Two and a half million light-years. Andromeda, another whole galaxy.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Humans have only existed for about three hundred thousand years.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Ten million light-years. Our whole local group of galaxies.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Now every speck around you is a galaxy.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: A hundred million light-years. Thousands of galaxies, strung together like a web.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Five hundred million light-years. Laniakea, the supercluster that holds us.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Between the threads, enormous voids. Nothing at all.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: A signal from your feet would now take longer than the universe has existed.
scenes.landmark_note: the age of the universe, in light
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Ninety three billion light-years. The edge of everything we can see.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: And you're still growing.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light

scenes.narration: Somewhere far below, on a street that no longer exists, your feet are still standing where you started.
scenes.gauge_label: Even at the speed of light
